findings.claim: SC-320 is an active acceptance scenario. It requires a non-zero exit and an identity-resolution error when the cwd has no git repo or remote. The superseded note (lines 70-80) says the opposite: there is no failure without an origin, and the directory name answers. The note marks only R-346 and R-347 as 'kept for the record'. SC-320 and the SC-322 precondition 'identity resolves to target-repo' have no such marker. A reader or test author who treats SC-320 as binding would implement behavior the owner decision removed. The intro rule (a requirement above this heading wins) does not cover this, because the superseding text sits inside this spec. This is copied faithfully from the source, so it is a carried-over inconsistency that the new canonical spec makes load-bearing.
